fullData.title: Finding an Equivalent Fraction on a Number Line
fullData.subject: Fractions

problem.statement: Use the number line below to help you find an equivalent fraction for $\frac{1}{2}$ that has a denominator of $8$. Look at where $\frac{1}{2}$ lands, and find the matching mark on the eighths scale.

fullData.solutionStrategy: Locate $\frac{1}{2}$ on the number line and read the fraction with denominator $8$ that shares the same position.

content.imagePrompt: A clean, colorful educational diagram of a unit number line from 0 to 1, divided into 8 equal parts with tick marks. The midpoint at 4/8 or 1/2 is highlighted with a bright indicator and labeled 1/2.
content.altText: A number line from 0 to 1 with eighths marked, highlighting the midpoint 1/2.

labels.description: The number line begins at zero and ends at one.
Find the spot right in the middle, which shows one-half.

annotations.steps: I located the point one-half right in the middle of the number line.
annotations.strategy: I notice that one-half is always the exact middle between zero and one.
annotations.misconceptions: Students sometimes think one-half belongs at the third tick mark because they miscount the spaces instead of the tick marks.
annotations.connections: This helps us see that many different fractions can name the exact same spot on a number line.
annotations.narrative: Find the point labeled $\frac{1}{2}$ on the number line, which sits at tick mark $0.5$.

transitions.operation: read matching mark on the eighths scale

challenge.prompt: When looking at the midpoint $\frac{1}{2}$ on a number line divided into eighths, which fraction matches that exact position?
challenge.rationale: One-half is halfway between 0 and 1, which corresponds to 4 out of 8 equal intervals ($\frac{4}{8}$), whereas $\frac{1}{8}$ keeps the numerator unchanged and $\frac{3}{8}$ comes from miscounting tick marks.

annotations.steps: Find the matching mark on the eighths scale at the same position as one-half.
annotations.strategy: I notice that different fraction scales can share the exact same spot on the number line.
annotations.misconceptions: Thinking that changing the denominator changes the position of the fraction on the number line.
annotations.connections: This connects to the idea that many different fractions can name the exact same amount.
annotations.narrative: At that same position of $0.5$, the matching mark on the eighths scale is $\frac{4}{8}$, so the equivalent fraction for $\frac{1}{2}$ with a denominator of $8$ is $\frac{4}{8}$.

specs.pedagogicalGoal: Recognize the benchmark fraction value of one-half as the midpoint on a unit number line.

specs.pedagogicalGoal: Connect identical positions on different fractional scales to establish fraction equivalence.
